lessons.title: Jesus’ Prayer for Unity
lessons.theme: On the eve of the cross, Jesus prayed for our unity

v: “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,
that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one,
I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me.

lessons.still: Imagine yourself sitting in the room of the Last Supper, listening to Jesus pray. He mentions “those who will believe in me through their word.” That means you. Quietly let the wonder of being remembered by the Lord fill you.
teach: What a person says just before parting often reveals what matters to them most. On the night he was betrayed, Jesus’ last long prayer was not mostly for himself. He prayed for his disciples, and for believers in every age, that they would “be one.” Unity was among the deepest burdens on Jesus’ heart.

Jesus’ prayer for unity has three layers. The source of unity is the triune God: “even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you.” The place of unity is in God: “that they also may be one in us.” The purpose of unity is gospel witness: “that the world may believe that you sent me.” Unity is not just an internal church matter; it is the way the world comes to know Jesus.

So division in the church is not only an internal problem; it is an obstacle to the gospel. When the world sees Christians loving one another, it sees God; when it sees Christians attacking one another, it cannot see God. A shift in mindset: unity is not an optional virtue but part of the Great Commission.
lessons.light: 321 Light: God’s kingdom system takes the unity of the triune God as its blueprint. When we let Jesus reign, he becomes the centre among us; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, we stop fighting for our own names. Unity is not something we manufacture; it is something we receive in God.
q: Who is God? — What kind of God do you see in the unity between the Father and the Son?
Who am I? — Jesus prayed for you that night too. How does that make you feel?
How shall I respond? — In your life, which broken relationship is standing in the way of the gospel?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not only pray for unity; he died for it. On the cross he broke down the dividing wall, making Jews and Gentiles one new humanity in himself. Our unity was bought with his precious blood.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you for praying for me on the night you were betrayed. Make us one, as you and the Father are one, so that the world may see from our love for one another that the Father sent you. And begin with me: help me mend the cracks where I am. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray John 17:21 over your church or fellowship
Pray a blessing over another church or fellowship
Reach out to a brother or sister you have not been in touch with for a long time
lessons.noon: “That they may all be one” — Lord, right now make my heart one with yours.

lessons.title: Self-Rule Breeds Conflict
lessons.theme: The root of conflict is not in others but in the desires within me

v: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?
for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?
For when one says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” aren’t you fleshly?

lessons.still: Recall your most recent argument. For now, set aside where the other person went wrong, and simply ask the Lord, “In that situation, what was I wanting to get?” Let the Holy Spirit shine on your own desires behind the conflict.
teach: Two hedgehogs on a freezing winter night want to keep each other warm. If they get too close, they prick each other; if they stay too far apart, they are cold. People are often like that. The problem is not closeness but the spines. If the spines are not dealt with, the closer the relationship, the deeper the wounds.

James asks bluntly: where do the fights and quarrels among you come from? The answer is not “because he went too far,” but “from your pleasures that war in your members.” Paul likewise says the jealousy and strife among the Corinthians showed they were “still fleshly.” Some said, “I follow Paul,” others, “I follow Apollos”; even spiritual leaders had become tools for comparison and taking sides.

The root of conflict is self-rule: I want it my way, I want to be valued, I want to win. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose. In a conflict, the most honest question is not “Who is right and who is wrong?” but “Who is reigning right now?” When I own up to my own desires, I truly open the door to unity.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Self-rule is the root of the fall and the root of conflict. If our focus is on others, we see only the spines on them; when our focus returns to Jesus, we see the spines on ourselves. A shift in mindset: from “It’s all their problem” to “Lord, change me first.”
q: Who is God? — Why does God go straight to the desires of the heart rather than dealing first with circumstances?
Who am I? — In your most recent conflict, what did you really want?
How shall I respond? — To whom will you admit your self-rule in a conflict?
lessons.jesus: At the Last Supper the disciples were still arguing about who was the greatest. Jesus did not join the debate. He got up, wrapped a towel around his waist and washed their feet. He answered their self-ruled quarrel with a self-emptied act.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that conflict often springs from the desires within me: wanting to be valued, wanting to win, wanting things my way. Pull out my spines, and help me see myself first in every conflict. Today I give up the throne to you. Please reign. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down what you really wanted in your most recent conflict
Go to the other person in that conflict and admit your part first
When you want to argue, pause for ten seconds and silently ask, “Who is reigning?”
lessons.noon: “Where do wars and fightings among you come from?” — Lord, right now search me first.

lessons.title: Eager to Keep Unity
lessons.theme: Unity is given by the Spirit, and we must work hard to keep it

v: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, even as you also were called in one hope of your calling,

lessons.still: Slowly say four words: humility, gentleness, patience, forbearance. After each one, pause and think of someone who needs you to treat them that way, and place them in the Lord’s hands.
teach: A precious porcelain heirloom does not stay intact for ever just because you own it. It needs to be placed with care, dusted regularly, and carefully wrapped when you move house. Unity is the same: it is a treasure God gives, and if we do not cherish and guard it, a single knock can crack it.

Paul speaks of keeping unity, not creating it. Unity is “of the Spirit”; we cannot manufacture it, only keep it. “Being eager” means it takes effort and cost. How do we keep it? Verses 2–3 list the ways: lowliness, humility, patience, bearing with one another in love, and the bond of peace. Verse 4 reminds us: there is one body and one Spirit.

Unity is not uniformity. It does not mean everyone thinks and acts the same, but that we keep one heart amid our differences, like different notes sounding together to make a beautiful chord. Keeping unity often means giving way on non-essentials, standing firm on essential truth, and holding on to love in all things.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Here the fruit of 920 is borne: humility, gentleness, patience, love and peace are all fruit of the Spirit. Keeping unity does not depend on technique but on a self-emptied life. People matter more than tasks: do not let who is right about one issue destroy the unity the Spirit has given.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit gives unity as a gift. What does this show you about him?
Who am I? — Of humility, gentleness, patience and forbearance, which do you lack most?
How shall I respond? — On which non-essential matter do you need to give way for the sake of unity?
lessons.jesus: Among Jesus’ disciples were Simon the Zealot and Matthew the tax collector, one who hated Rome and one who collected taxes for Rome. Yet Jesus put them on the same team. In him, people on opposite sides learned to bear with one another.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for the gift of unity. Make me humble, gentle and patient in all things, bearing with others in love and bound to them in peace. I am willing to give way in small things; make me stand firm in the truth, and help me hold on to love in everything. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Give way on one non-essential matter, and do it with joy
Say a word of appreciation to someone whose personality is very different from yours
Before you speak today, ask yourself: will this build connection or tear down?
lessons.noon: “Being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” — Lord, right now make me a messenger of unity.

lessons.title: Humility Draws Out Humility
lessons.theme: Counting others better than ourselves opens the door to unity

v: make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.

lessons.still: Think of someone you often secretly feel you are better than. Before the Lord, honestly count three ways in which they are better than you, and let this exercise slowly soften your heart.
teach: Two cars meet in a narrow lane. Neither will back up, so neither can get through. If just one of them reverses a few metres, both can pass. Humility looks like losing out, but in fact it lets both sides move forward. Pride provokes pride; humility draws out humility.

Paul urges the Philippian church to be “like-minded, having the same love,” and his method is very concrete: do nothing out of rivalry or conceit, but in humility “each counting others better than himself,” “not just looking to his own things, but … also to the things of others.” This is not putting ourselves down; it is choosing to see God’s grace in others and to take their needs to heart.

In the Philippian church two sisters, Euodia and Syntyche, needed to be reconciled (4:2). Paul did not rule on who was right. He brought them before the heart of Christ. Unity often begins when one side humbles itself first. Do not wait for the other person to change first. Humble people take the initiative to reverse, to apologise and to bless, and so they open the way for both sides to win.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility is the key to revival, and the key to unity. Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win. When we lay down power and return to our place, letting people be people and letting God be God, relationships are healed.
q: Who is God? — What does Christ’s self-emptying heart show you about how God treats people?
Who am I? — Do you often wait for others to give way or apologise first?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship will you be the first to “reverse” today?
lessons.jesus: Though Jesus existed in the form of God, he emptied himself and became a servant. He did not wait for others to humble themselves first; he humbled himself first, all the way down to the cross. This Lord who humbled himself first has drawn countless people into humility and reconciliation.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you humbled yourself first, you lowered yourself first, you gave yourself first. Help me stop waiting for others to change first. Instead, let me be humble first, count others better than myself, and look to their interests too. Let my humility draw out humility, so that your body wins together. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three ways in which someone you often compare yourself with is better than you
Take the first step towards healing a relationship that is stuck
At least once today, put someone else’s needs before your own
lessons.noon: “Each counting others better than himself” — Lord, right now let me be the first to humble myself.

lessons.title: Only the Self-Emptied Can Be One
lessons.theme: All one in Christ, bound together by love, the bond of perfection

v: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free man, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.

lessons.still: Quietly say, “Lord, I am in you, and they are in you too.” Think of a brother or sister who is very different from you, place the two of you together in the Lord’s embrace, and rest there for a moment.
teach: A pile of planks, each holding on to its own shape, is just a pile of wood. Only when they are willing to be planed, cut to fit and joined together do they become a table. Unity does not mean each plank disappears; it means each finds its place in a greater design. That is the self-emptied life: not ceasing to exist, but entering a greater whole.

Galatians 3:28 says that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female; we are all one. The differences remain, but they are no longer dividing walls. Colossians calls love “the bond of perfection,” like a belt that ties all the virtues together. It also says, “let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts.” The word “rule” originally meant “to act as umpire”: when conflict arises, let Christ’s peace make the final call.

This week we have seen Jesus’ prayer for unity (Day 1), how self-rule breeds conflict (Day 2), being eager to keep unity (Day 3) and how humility draws out humility (Day 4). Today it all comes down to one sentence: only the self-emptied can be one. Only when each of us steps down from our own throne can Christ take his seat in our midst. Next week we will see that a united church is a vessel for the coming of the kingdom.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Only through the self-emptied life can we be one and overcome. Self-ruled people have a hundred centres, so they cannot get along; self-emptied people have only one centre: Christ. When we let Jesus reign, we live in one kingdom together; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, we no longer need to fight for ourselves.
q: Who is God? — What does being “all one” in Christ show you about God’s heart?
Who am I? — What invisible wall in your heart still shuts certain people out?
How shall I respond? — In which conflict will you let Christ’s peace be the umpire today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus talked with the Samaritan woman at the well, crossing three high walls at once: race, gender and morality. He did not require her to become a Jew first; he offered her living water first. In him, every dividing wall can be torn down.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, in you we are all one. Tear down the invisible walls in my heart, help me walk in love, and let your peace rule in my heart. I step down from my own throne. Take your seat in our midst, and make us one in heart and mind, to the glory of your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Greet and bless a brother or sister whose background is very different from yours
When opinions differ, first ask for Christ’s peace to rule, then speak
Pray with a spiritual companion for the unity of your church
lessons.noon: “For you are all one in Christ Jesus.” — Lord, right now empty me of self and make me one with all the saints.
